land.text: the former sultanate, from Zequalla to Zeila

successors.note: Dawit I defeated Ifat's troops on the Harar plateau in 1403 and pursued the sultan to Zeila (Ifat page; the Ethiopian Empire page: the sultanate ended when Zeila was captured). Whether Ethiopian officials ruled the land until 1415 is not on the pages.
In 1415 Sabr ad-Din III, son of Sa'ad ad-Din II, returned from exile in Arabia and founded Adal (Adal page); the same dynasty, but the Ifat page and Cliopatria treat them as two states.

capitals.name: Wafat (site not given)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Wafat (1275-1387)'. No page opened gives the site; the dot is on the Harar plateau, where the page says Haqq ad-Din II transferred the capital in the fourteenth century (undated). Coordinates are those of Harar in the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Zeila
capitals.note: Infobox 'Zeila (1387-1403)'. Coordinates are the researcher's (Zeila is in the gazetteer).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1285 shape taken back to the infobox date; the page names no earlier extent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1275-1284. The Ifat infobox gives 'Established: 1275' (with 'Ali Baziwi 1275-1299' in the sultan table) while Cliopatria and the Shewa page start the Walashma dynasty's rule in 1285. The page gives no extent before the conquest of Shewa, so Cliopatria's 1285 shape is carried back; confidence 1.

121,451 km2 against the infobox 'Total: 120,000 km2' (no year): ratio 1.01. The page: 'The polity stretched from Zequalla to the port city of Zeila'; Huntingford put 'southern and eastern boundaries ... along the Awash River'. The Sultanate of Shewa page: 'In 1285 Ali b. Wali Asma deposed the kings of Shewa', and Shewa then became 'one of the seven districts of the Ifat sultanate'.

120,851 km2, nearly the same shape. The Amda Seyon page: in 1332 Sabr ad-Din 'surrendered himself to Amda Seyon's camp' and the emperor appointed Jamal ad-Din I, then Nasir ad-Din, as governor; the Ifat page calls the sultan a 'vassal king under Amde Seyon'. The shape is unchanged because the land stayed Ifat's, as a vassal (the Ethiopian Empire dossier carries the vassal tint). Holds 1333-1402.

correction.text: the same outline, but after 1403 it is drawn in the ethiopian-empire dossier, not as Ifat

keyframe_review.note: The shape (120,851 km2, the same as 1333) is drawn for 1407-1414, but the Ifat page has the sultanate ending in 1403 ('Ifat's troops were defeated in 1403 on the Harar plateau'; infobox 'Disestablished: 1403'; another source puts Sa'ad ad-Din II's death in 1410). The land belongs to the Ethiopian Empire's keyframe ethiopian-empire_1404 until the Walashma return in 1415 (Adal page). Shape unchanged, years wrong.

region.text: Ifat in the Awash and Harar highlands

ledger.note: 1275: the Sultanate of Ifat is founded (infobox 'Established: 1275'). The page's table gives Umar 1197-1276 and Ali 'Baziwi' 1275-1299, and 'Umar died around 1275' per Maqrizi; the Sultanate of Shewa page dates the Walashma dynasty of Ifat 1285-1415. The page names no extent before 1285, so the region is Cliopatria's 1285 shape.

region.text: the Sultanate of Shewa, capital Walalah in northern Hararghe

ledger.note: 1285: Ifat conquers the Sultanate of Shewa. 'In 1285 Ali b. Wali Asma deposed the kings of Shewa and installed a certain MHz.' (infobox 'Shewa conquered by Ifat: 1278-1285'). Shewa had its capital at Walalah in northern Hararghe and 'extended possibly to areas west of the Awash River'; it became one of seven districts of Ifat.

region.text: Hubat, Zeila and other Muslim states

ledger.counterpart: Hubat, Zeila and other Muslim states
ledger.note: 1288: Ifat imposes its rule on the coast. 'In 1288 Sultan Wali Asma successfully imposed his rule on Hubat, Zeila and other Muslim states.'

1299: Ifat and the Ethiopian emperor Wedem Arad quarrel over eastern Shewa ('in conflict with the Sultanate of Ifat over eastern Shewa'). The Ifat page dates the conflict between the Christian monarch and the Ifat leaders to 1320 ('In 1320 a conflict between the Christian monarch and Muslim Ifat leaders began').

1332: Ifat's rebellion is crushed. 'Sabr ad-Din's rebellion in early 1332' (Ifat page); Sabr ad-Din 'surrendered himself to Amda Seyon's camp' (Amda Seyon page). Ifat stays as a vassal; the Ethiopian Empire dossier carries the vassal tint 1332-1403.
1387: the capital moves to Zeila (infobox: Zeila 1387-1403).
1403: Dawit I takes the sultanate. The pages say the sultanate ended; neither says the Ethiopian Empire ruled the land until 1415, so the transfer is a bridge.

1403: Ifat falls. 'After much war, Ifat's troops were defeated in 1403 on the Harar plateau'; Maqrizi has Dawit I pursuing the sultan to Zeila where Sa'ad ad-Din II was executed ('no other contemporary source corroborates the invasion of Zeila' - Adal page); another source dates his death to 1410. The Walashma return and found Adal in 1415.

wars.name: Ethiopian-Ifat wars of Amda Seyon
wars.outcome: Ifat was defeated in 1332 and became an Ethiopian vassal; the emperor appointed Jamal ad-Din I and later Nasir ad-Din as governor.
wars.note: Ifat page: conflict began 1320; Sabr ad-Din's rebellion in early 1332. Amda Seyon page: 1332 is 'the generally accepted year' (Huntingford favoured 1329).

wars.name: Dawit I's invasion of Ifat
wars.outcome: Ifat's troops were defeated on the Harar plateau in 1403 and the sultan pursued to Zeila; the sultanate ended.
wars.note: The other source gives 1410 for Sa'ad ad-Din II's death, crediting Yeshaq.

certainty.note: Only the Awash and the coast are named by the pages; Huntingford's boundaries are 'provisional'.

notes:
Cliopatria's Ifat row (1285..1414) is one state on the Wikipedia page, so it is not split. Start moved back to the infobox 1275 (new keyframe, confidence 1); end moved from 1414 to 1403 (infobox; another source 1410). Cliopatria's 1407 shape (1407-1414) is marked wrong; the land is the Ethiopian Empire's from 1404 (ethiopian-empire_1404) until the Walashma refounded Adal in 1415.

Disagreements: 1275 (infobox) vs 1285 (Shewa page: Walashma rule of Ifat 1285-1415); Ifat's wars with Ethiopia dated 1299 (Ethiopian Empire page) and 1320 (Ifat page); the Amda Seyon campaign 1332 vs 1329; Sa'ad ad-Din II's death 1403 vs 1410. The Ifat page's sultan table gives mostly unknown reign years, so no ruler list is written. Capital 'Wafat' has no site on the pages (the dot is on the Harar plateau); the move to the Harar plateau in the fourteenth century is undated.

Needs dossiers: sultanate-of-shewa (896..1286 on its page; conquered 1285), a counterpart of af-01-a's list. Region names needed by the gazetteer: none new beyond the Ethiopian Empire dossier (Hubat appears only in a text field).
